editor_note: Both rewritten headings keep the English meaning and read naturally. "File ng configuration ng user" (entry 4) and "Mga environment variable" (entry 18) match the "environment variable na `QISKIT_SETTINGS`" usage in the body text.

The meaning holds throughout. The beta caveat in [22], the override behavior in [25]/[26] and the level-2 "not guaranteed zero-bias" caveat in [20] all come through correctly. Entry [17], the core explanation of resilience levels, has several literal calques a native editor would rewrite. "At the expense of" became "sa gastos ng", "build resilience" became "itatayo", and "abstracts" became the awkward hybrid "nag-aabstract". Terminology is consistent: resilience level becomes "antas ng resilience", and noise management and circuit are kept in English.

examples.line_approx: Ang mas mataas na antas ay nagbubuo ng mas tumpak na mga resulta, sa gastos ng mas matagal na oras ng pagproseso.
examples.source: Higher levels generate more accurate results, at the expense of longer processing times.
examples.translation: ...sa gastos ng mas matagal na oras ng pagproseso.
examples.suggested: Mas tumpak ang resulta sa mas mataas na antas, kapalit ng mas matagal na oras ng pagproseso.
examples.why: 'sa gastos ng' is a word-for-word calque of 'at the expense of'. The idiomatic Tagalog is 'kapalit ng'.

examples.line_approx: Tinutukoy ng `resilience_level` kung gaano karaming resilience ang itatayo laban sa mga error.
examples.source: specifies how much resilience to build against errors
examples.translation: kung gaano karaming resilience ang itatayo laban sa mga error
examples.suggested: kung gaano kalakas ang proteksyon laban sa mga error
examples.why: 'itatayo' (to erect or construct) is a literal rendering of 'build' that sounds odd in this context.

examples.line_approx: Ang antas ng resilience ay nag-aabstract ng detalyadong pagpili ng pamamaraan
examples.source: The resilience level abstracts the detailed choice of noise management method
examples.suggested: Itinatago ng antas ng resilience ang detalye ng pagpili ng pamamaraan ng noise management, para makapagpasya ang mga gumagamit...
examples.why: The Taglish verb 'nag-aabstract' is stiff and unclear to learners. 'Itinatago ang detalye' explains the idea better.

editor_note: The rewritten heading [3], "Pagbo-broadcast ng Executor", is accurate and doesn't mislead, but it no longer matches the page title [1], "Broadcasting ng Executor". "Pagbo-broadcast" is a natural Tagalog form, but using it only in the H1 makes the page title and the visible heading disagree. Changing it back to "Broadcasting ng Executor" keeps the page consistent.

examples.suggested: Broadcasting ng Executor {#executor-broadcasting}

editor_note: Entries 25 and 26 are faithful: they keep the 28-day rolling window, keep pending workloads in the queue while active and session-mode ones run ("gayunpaman, ang anumang aktibong workload ay magpapatuloy... kabilang ang mga workload sa session mode"), keep the "hindi limited" to lower priority condition, and match the wording of entry 20.

Entry 20 is faithful and reads naturally. Every bullet keeps its meaning: "Alamin kung paano bumuo ng OpenQASM code sa gabay na [IBM Quantum Composer]" and "Bisitahin ang paksang [I-verify ang iyong programa]", with "Mga Rekomendasyon" as the title and casual register throughout.

Entry 1 (title) is faithful and needs no change. Entry 22 (the "Paunawa" disclaimer) keeps all three claims and the hedging ("Maaaring", "Sa ilang kaso"), but two things should change. It drops "therefore", so the closing recommendation no longer follows from the caveat before it. Also, "sa parehong problem instance at ..." can be read as "on the same problem instance" instead of "on both the problem instance and ...". Neither mistake would mislead a learner.

examples.source: Evaluation should therefore consider the complete optimization workflow.
examples.translation: Dapat isaalang-alang ng ebalwasyon ang kumpletong optimization workflow.
examples.suggested: Kaya dapat isaalang-alang ng ebalwasyon ang buong optimization workflow.
examples.why: The word "therefore" was dropped, so the recommendation no longer reads as following from the caveat before it. This is a dropped qualifier, not a false claim.

examples.source: Performance can depend on both the problem instance and subsequent processing steps.
examples.translation: Maaaring depende ang performance sa parehong problem instance at kasunod na mga hakbang sa pagproseso.
examples.suggested: Maaaring nakadepende ang performance kapwa sa problem instance at sa mga kasunod na hakbang sa pagproseso.
examples.why: "sa parehong problem instance" can be read as "on the same problem instance". Using "kapwa ... at sa ..." makes "both" clear and also reads more naturally.

editor_note: Neither rewritten entry misleads the learner. Entry 30, "Mga Fake backend", is fine and matches "fake backend" in entries 25, 29 and 31. Entry 40 changes the heading to "Simulation ng Clifford", but the text under it keeps "Clifford simulation" ("ang Clifford simulation" in entry 41, "Clifford simulation mode" in entry 34, "Clifford Simulation" in the table in entry 28). The heading should use the same term as its section. "Simulation ng Clifford" is also a bit ambiguous, because it can read as simulating something called "Clifford" instead of naming the method.

examples.source: Clifford simulation {#clifford-simulation}
examples.suggested: Clifford simulation {#clifford-simulation}

The genitive form 'Simulation ng Clifford' also makes the name of the method read like 'simulation of Clifford'. This is a minor inconsistency and does not mislead.

editor_note: Entry 14 is accurate overall. The caveat 'walang iisang distribution ... ang tiyak na nagmamay-ari ng lahat ng naka-install na file' matches 'no one distribution ... necessarily owns all the installed files'. The closing clause has two problems. 'ang ganap na pag-uninstall o i-upgrade ito' joins a noun (pag-uninstall) to a verb (i-upgrade), so the parallel structure breaks. The trailing 'ito' also reads as the namespace package, while the English 'one' means one distribution. A reader can still work out the meaning, so this is a naturalness issue and would not mislead.

examples.source: so it can be tricky to completely uninstall or upgrade one.
examples.translation: kaya maaaring maging mahirap ang ganap na pag-uninstall o i-upgrade ito.
examples.suggested: kaya maaaring maging mahirap ang ganap na pag-uninstall o pag-upgrade ng isa sa mga ito.
examples.why: The noun 'pag-uninstall' is joined to the verb 'i-upgrade', which breaks the parallel structure. 'ito' also shifts the referent from 'one (distribution)' to the namespace package.

editor_note: The meaning is faithful throughout and nothing here would mislead a learner. The twirling-precedence rule in [20], the seed_estimator caveat in [22] and the noise-learning requirement for PEA/PEC in [26]-[27] all carry over correctly. A native editor would still fix a few things. The Admonition in [27] drops the bold on "**require**", which weakens the emphasis. "mas hindi episyente" in [38] is a stiff calque. The page uses "directed execution model" everywhere else but renders it "Modelo ng directed execution" in [58]. "may dalang" in [56] drops "still".

examples.source: Submitting A and C as separate jobs is less efficient

examples.suggested: ...bilang magkahiwalay na job ay hindi gaanong episyente
examples.why: 'mas hindi episyente' is a literal calque of 'less efficient'. 'hindi gaanong episyente' is the natural Tagalog phrasing.

examples.source: Directed execution model
examples.suggested: Directed execution model
examples.why: Entries [7] and [8] keep 'directed execution model' as a single term. Translating it only in the link list is inconsistent.

examples.source: A PUB that still carries a parameter-values array fails coercion.

examples.suggested: Ang isang PUB na may dala pa ring parameter-values array ay mabibigo sa coercion.

editor_note: Entry 11 is faithful and natural: "Kunin ang natatanging identifier ng job" and "Mag-block hanggang maabot ng job ang terminal state" keep the meaning, and it correctly leaves "blocking call" and "terminal state" in English as programming terms.

editor_note: Entry 19 keeps the meaning of the English. The tuple order `(input_dim, output_dim)` and the caveat that it is the reverse of the matrix shape ("kabaligtaran ng hugis ng pinagbabatayan na matrix") are both intact. One small slip: "ang output ay ibinalik" uses the completed aspect (past tense), but the English "is returned" describes what always happens. A native editor would write "ibinabalik" here.

examples.source: *Note: the output is returned as a tuple* `(input_dim, output_dim)`
examples.translation: *Tandaan: ang output ay ibinalik bilang tuple* `(input_dim, output_dim)`
examples.suggested: *Tandaan: ibinabalik ang output bilang tuple* `(input_dim, output_dim)`
examples.why: 'Ibinalik' is the completed aspect, so it reads as a single event in the past. The English describes what the property always returns, so the incompleted/habitual 'ibinabalik' is the natural choice.

editor_note: Rewritten entries 64 and 65 are faithful and natural: "Review the ... API" becomes "Suriin ang [`qiskit-ibm-runtime` Estimator/Sampler] API", with the links, code spans and Admonition markup left intact and the Estimator/Sampler names kept in English as they are elsewhere in the file.

Entry 167's rewritten heading "Complex-valued na amplitude" means the same as the English and matches the "complex-valued pulse amplitude" wording in the next entry (168), so it is faithful and consistent.

Entry 107 keeps the English meaning. The invalid environment mixing 1.0+ with an older version, the advice not to mix pre-1.0 and post-1.0 dependencies, the note that packages depending on 'qiskit-terra' must be updated ("kailangang i-update"), and the caveat that Qiskit cannot enforce this during resolution ("hindi kayang ipatupad ... habang nireresolba") are all rendered correctly. The one problem is that this entry is the literal ImportError text Qiskit prints, introduced in entry 106 as "you might see an error such as:". Because it is translated, learners cannot match it or search for the error they actually see in their terminal. The same page keeps error strings verbatim elsewhere ("ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'qiskit'" in entry 82 and "AttributeError: module 'qiskit' has no attribute" in entry 86), so the English text should be kept, perhaps with a Tagalog gloss.

examples.source: ImportError: Qiskit is installed in an invalid environment that has both Qiskit 1.0+ and an earlier version. ...
examples.translation: ImportError: Naka-install ang Qiskit sa isang invalid environment na may parehong Qiskit 1.0+ at mas lumang bersyon. ...
examples.suggested: Keep the error message in English exactly as Qiskit prints it (as entries 82 and 86 do). If needed, add a short Tagalog explanation outside the quoted output.
examples.why: This is literal program output. Qiskit never prints the Tagalog version, so learners cannot recognize or search for the message they actually get. The meaning of the translation is correct.

editor_note: Rewritten entry 44, "Halimbawa ng paggamit ng licensed function", keeps the English heading's meaning and matches the "licensed na user" / "license token" wording in entry 45 that follows it.

Rewritten heading [23] correctly keeps the established English term "Dynamical Decoupling", matching "dynamical decoupling" in [22] and the kept "Twirling" in [24]; its title-case capital is left to the deterministic capitalization sweep.

Entry 11's heading "Arkitektura ng Instruction Set" is a faithful, natural Tagalog rendering, and it lines up with the body text in entry 12, which keeps the English term "Instruction Set Architecture (ISA)".

editor_note: None of the five rewritten entries would mislead a learner. Entry 161 keeps the meaning, including the caveat that there is "walang simpleng recipe" and the "sining ng quantum code design" framing. The four rewritten headings (25, 37, 44, 49) now use English-style Title Case plus an inserted linker ("3-bit na Repetition Code", "9-qubit na Shor Code", "7-qubit na Steane Code", "5-qubit na Code"). That clashes with the sibling headings, which use sentence case ([34] "Binagong 3-bit repetition code", [53] "Mga one-dimensional na stabilizer code"). It also clashes with the body, which names these codes without "na" ("ang 3-bit repetition code", "ang 5-qubit code"). "5-qubit na Code" reads especially stiff because it is a proper name (the 5-qubit code), not a description.

examples.source: 3-bit repetition code
examples.suggested: 3-bit repetition code
examples.why: Title Case and the inserted 'na' clash with sibling heading [34] 'Binagong 3-bit repetition code' and with the body's 'ang 3-bit repetition code'. The same pattern appears in [37] and [44] ('9-qubit na Shor Code', '7-qubit na Steane Code').

examples.source: 5-qubit code
examples.suggested: 5-qubit code
examples.why: The English is the conventional name of a specific code, which [52] renders as 'ang 5-qubit code'. Adding 'na' and a capitalized 'Code' turns the name into an awkward generic description.

editor_note: Entry 12 matches the English in meaning. The data shared (pangalan, email address, badge na nakuha), Credly's US location, the "Maaaring ibahagi" permission and the global sharing with subsidiaries and third parties are all kept, and nothing is added. One wording choice needs fixing: "IBM privacy practices" is rendered as "mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM". "Kasanayan" mainly means "skills", and entry 0 of this same page uses it that way ("mga kasanayan sa quantum algorithms"), so it reads awkwardly here. "Mga patakaran" or "mga pamamaraan sa privacy" would express "practices" (the policies IBM follows) more clearly.

examples.source: It will be handled in a manner consistent with IBM privacy practices.
examples.translation: Pangangasiwaan ito nang naaayon sa mga kasanayan sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.suggested: Pangangasiwaan ito nang naaayon sa mga patakaran sa privacy ng IBM.
examples.why: 'Kasanayan' mainly means 'skill', and entry 0 uses it that way. For 'practices' in the sense of an organization's procedures, 'patakaran' or 'pamamaraan' is the natural choice.

editor_note: Entry 82 means the same as the English and would not mislead a learner. The problem is that the heading uses the Tagalog "Notasyong", while the section it introduces keeps the English word "notation" throughout ("Big-O notation", "notation na ito" in [84], [87], [88], [91], [92]). The heading also capitalizes "Asymptotic" mid-phrase, although every other heading in the file uses sentence case (e.g. "Mga encoding at haba ng input"). "Notasyong asymptotic" or "Asymptotic notation" would fix both.

examples.source: Asymptotic notation {#asymptotic-notation}
examples.suggested: Notasyong asymptotic {#asymptotic-notation}

The mid-heading capital 'Asymptotic' also breaks the file's sentence-case headings. Meaning is intact, so this is minor.

Both rewritten headings are faithful and defensible: [109] keeps "Superdense Coding" as the established English protocol name, and [127] "Teorema ng Hughston-Jozsa-Wootters" matches the page's "Teorema" figure title and reads naturally.

examples.suggested: Quantum computing {#quantum-computing}

editor_note: None of the 7 rewritten entries would mislead a learner, but a native editor would still fix several things. In entry 44 the prose line "We now determine the eigenvalues:" was left in English. In entry 111, "$\it{ilang}$ orthonormal na basis" reads as "a few/several bases" when the English means "any arbitrary basis" (use "anumang"), and "eigenvalue ng interes" is a calque. The headings in 121 and 156 render "Time evolution" as "Ebolusyon ng Oras" ("evolution of time"), which clashes with "time evolution" in the body (entries 118, 122). Those two headings and 141 ("Generalized na Eigenvalue Problem") also use Title Case, while the rest of the page uses sentence case. Entry 12 has the calque "nakabuo sa paligid ng" and mixes "method"/"lesson" with the page's usual "paraan ng Krylov"/"aralin".

examples.line_approx: between the matrix and the determinant equation
examples.source: We now determine the eigenvalues:
examples.suggested: Tukuyin natin ngayon ang mga eigenvalue:

editor_note: Five of the six rewritten entries are faithful and read naturally. That includes entry 49's contrast between SKQD and SQD ("garantiya ng convergence na wala ang SQD", "variational component", "pamilya ng mga ansaetze") and the title rendering "Diagonalization ng Krylov Quantum na Batay sa Sample", which is a defensible choice. Entry 50 drops the intensifier from "much less QPU time" and gives just "mas kaunting QPU time", so SKQD's advantage over KQD comes across weaker than in the English. editor_note: None of the four rewritten entries misleads a learner. Entries 10, 23 and 86 are faithful ("Dataset ng Training", "Target na Circuit", "i-transpile natin ... nang 20 beses"). Entry 76 keeps the key caveat that 100% accuracy is not quantum advantage, but it has two wording problems. First, "characterizing different data types" is rendered as "pag-uuri", which means sorting or classifying. That is a poor word choice on a page about classification, because it blurs the research task with the ML task itself. Second, "nagpapaghinala sa iyo" is an awkward, barely idiomatic causative.

examples.source: There is much work to be done characterizing different data types and data relationships
examples.translation: Marami pang gawaing dapat gawin sa pag-uuri ng iba't ibang uri ng data at relasyon ng data
examples.suggested: Marami pang dapat gawin sa pagkilala sa mga katangian ng iba't ibang uri ng data at ng mga relasyon nito
examples.why: 'pag-uuri' means sorting or classifying, not characterizing. On a classification page this blurs the research task with the ML task itself. The sentence's point still gets through, so this is minor.

examples.source: What structure in your data makes you suspect that a quantum feature map is useful?
examples.translation: Anong istraktura sa iyong data ang nagpapaghinala sa iyo na kapaki-pakinabang ang isang quantum feature map?
examples.suggested: Anong istraktura sa iyong data ang nagpapahiwatig sa iyo na maaaring kapaki-pakinabang ang isang quantum feature map?
examples.why: 'nagpapaghinala' is an awkward, nonstandard causative. A native technical writer would use 'nagpapahiwatig' or 'nagbibigay-dahilan para isipin'.

editor_note: Entry 51 is faithful and reads naturally. "kahit hindi ito nangyari sa simulator" keeps the contrast with the simulator, "Dahil may noise ang mga tunay na device" keeps the cause, "paminsan-minsang mga error" keeps "occasional", and "mga gate at sukat" matches how entry 39 renders measurements.

None of the 7 rewritten entries changes the meaning. Entry 145 correctly keeps the argument that no coefficients a0, a1, b0, b1 exist, so the Bell state is an "entangled state". The issues are wording only. Entry 21 uses "kung saan" twice in one clause ("kung saan ang α at β ay mga complex number kung saan ..."), which is stiff. Entry 167's heading "GHZ na estado" clashes with "GHZ state" in the body (entries 168 and 175), and entry 123 "Multi-qubit na quantum gates" keeps the English plural "-s" with no "mga", unlike the file's usual "mga ... gate". The file also mixes "Multi-qubit na quantum circuit" (entry 103) with "Multi-qubit quantum gate" (entry 102), and entry 28 opens with the formula but has no "Ang" before it.

examples.source: where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are complex numbers such that $|\alpha|^2+|\beta|^2=1$.

examples.why: Using "kung saan" twice in one clause reads like machine translation. The second one should be a relative clause instead.
